To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) the number of light sources required for accurate photometric stereo is independent of scattering and (b) light stripe scanning can be made robust to scattering by using multiple exposures.

(a) light striping can be made to work in scattering environments, and (b) for photometric stereo to work in scattering environment, one needs to use a larger number of light sources and a more complex model for the surface reflectance

(1) structured lighting methods are not affected by scattering if (a) the source is point-like and the detector is small enough, and (b) there are at least three independent measurements, and (2) the appearance of a scene in a structured lighting system is a function of the scattering properties of the medium as well as the scene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of structured light methods for underwater and aerial imaging.
the development of structured light methods that are robust to scattering and can thus be used in underwater and aerial applications.
the fundamental question of how to design and analyze structured light methods in the presence of light scattering.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
structured light methods can be extended for underwater imaging.
the proposed method is able to recover the scene as well as the scattering properties of the medium, and to restore the appearances as if they were acquired in clear air.
the structured light methods are not only robust to the scattering but can be used to recover the properties of the scattering media.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the physical models we have derived are general enough to be used for other methods, and the results we have obtained can be used for the design and analysis of other structured lighting methods in scattering media.
structured lighting can be used in a wide range of environments, from clear air to highly scattering and absorbing media.
we provide the first comprehensive analysis and results of structured light methods for imaging in scattering media.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of scattering can be modeled and accounted for to achieve accurate and robust results.
scattering effects are not a hindrance to structured lighting, and can be exploited to improve the quality of the recovered data.
structured light methods can be used for imaging in scattering environments, and that the key to success lies in a careful analysis of the underlying physics.
